title: DSL node groups as a library with a node tree: path-addressed inspection and overrides, the quad layout as a DSL group, and scenes that feed their model into it
description:
Agreed with the user 2026-09-26 during the tool review of the quad-layout PATCH session (ai-workspace/reports/tool-review-2026-09-20.md, Rulings, items 1 and 11). Problem: to learn anything about one element of a pipeline run (a trace, an arc, a node), agents add log lines, public counters and describe/dump helpers to the source, and those land. PATCH-115 as published carried 934 lines of that next to a 289-line fix. And changing one node input (NDirectionField curvature_bias) led first to a system property and then to a scene key, both rejected. The user wants one general mechanism for any node in any graph, not a quad-layout route and not more run-scene flags (two NDirectionField nodes would already break a flag keyed by node type).

WHAT EXISTS. (a) DSL functions are node groups: `def name(param: TYPE, ...) -> TYPE: ... end`, callable from graphs and from other functions (NodeGraphRuntime.executeFunctionCall, resources/dsl/test_function.dsl). (b) NodeGraphRuntime.executeGraphResult takes overrides keyed `<nodeId>.<port>` (plus `.x/.y/.z` for vectors), fed by GraphChoice.overrides. (c) SkillLibrary loads `.skill` files of DSL function definitions (resources/skills/subdivided_cube.skill), but only ValidateDsl uses it; no scene's runtime loads it. (d) ModelScene is the shared base of the quad-layout scenes; it resolves a model through ModelCatalog (the `ixdar.model` launch property, the model menu, the `ml` terminal command, TOOL-11's `ixdar-cli model`), loads it into halfEdgeMesh, and handles `graph:` choices (GraphChoice DSL fixtures, used by EmbeddedTMeshScene).

WHAT IS MISSING. Inside a group call the body nodes live in a local map and are discarded; the call returns only its last node's outputs, so a group has one output, no per-inner-node timing, and no way to address an inner node. The runtime also discards every MeshNode instance after evaluate() and keeps only its outputs. Overrides are flat ids, cannot address a node inside one particular group call, and an unknown key is silently ignored, so a parameter sweep can quietly do nothing. Groups must be defined in the file that calls them. QuadLayoutEngine is the only MeshNode that builds and evaluates other MeshNodes in Java (via .with(...)), which makes the quad-layout pipeline a node group the runtime cannot see into. /mesh/dsl/timing only works on MeshNodeViewerScene.

HOW THE SCENES USE THE PIPELINE TODAY. Five ModelScenes each load the model and then run a hand-picked prefix of QuadLayoutEngine in Java: cross-field-exam calls buildCrossField, param-exam buildCrossField and buildSeamless, mcg-exam buildMotorcycleGraph, quad-layout the whole engine (rendering from engine.seamless, engine.globalGrid, engine.patchSurfaces and engine.patchCoons), embedded-tmesh the T-mesh stages plus DSL fixtures through GraphChoice. mesh-viewer runs an arbitrary DSL chosen by the ixdar.mesh.dsl system property.

THE DESIGN.
1. Node tree. The runtime records one entry per evaluated node, including every node inside a group call: its path, type, MeshNode instance, inputs and outputs, wall time, peak heap and children. The path is the call-site ids joined with `/`: `layout/motorcycle`. `.` keeps separating a node from its port, and a vector port from its component.
2. Inspection. A generic route and CLI command, e.g. `ixdar-cli node-inspect` with no argument prints the tree (path, type, ms, peak MiB, indented), `node-inspect layout/motorcycle` shows that node's inputs, outputs and public fields, and `node-inspect layout/motorcycle traces[127].state` walks public fields reflectively with depth and list-length limits. It works on the active ModelScene's runtime, whatever the scene. /mesh/dsl/timing reads the same tree and also stops being tied to MeshNodeViewerScene.
3. Group inputs, as in Blender. Values meant to vary are group parameters with defaults: `def quad_layout(geometry: GEOMETRY_BUNDLE, alpha_degrees: FLOAT = 15.0, curvature_bias: FLOAT = -1.0) -> ...`. Instances of a group differ only through their inputs; the group's body is shared.
4. Path overrides for debugging. `layout/field.curvature_bias=-0.5` sets one inner node's port in one call without editing the group. An override whose path or port does not exist fails and lists the nearest real paths.
5. Named group outputs, like Blender's Group Output node: a group declares several named outputs (the stage results a scene draws), and callers read them as ports of the call.
6. Group library. Group definitions live in their own files under resources (SkillLibrary's `.skill` format or plain `.dsl`, one mechanism) and every NodeGraphRuntime loads them, so a graph calls `quad_layout(...)` without defining it.
7. The quad layout as a DSL group. QuadLayoutEngine's stage chaining becomes a library group over the nodes that already exist (cross_field, seamless_uv, motorcycle_graph, arc_quantization, layout_embedding, tmesh_contract, integer_grid_map, plus the patch-surface step), under the name quad_layout so resources/dsl/fertility_quad_layout.dsl keeps working. Then no MeshNode builds or evaluates another MeshNode; enforce that with a check (an autofix checkstyle rule, or a unit test over the node registry).
8. How scenes run it and feed their model in. Each ModelScene that shows the pipeline runs a small scene graph through NodeGraphRuntime instead of calling engine methods. The model enters the graph through a scene-bound input node, e.g. `model = scene_model()`, whose output is the GeometryBundle of the mesh ModelScene already loaded, so model choice keeps going through ModelCatalog (launch property, menu, ml, ixdar-cli model, collections) and the graph never hardcodes a path; standalone graphs keep using load_mesh(path=...). The scene's graph is a resource per scene, e.g. `model = scene_model()` then `layout = quad_layout(geometry=model.geometry)`. A model switch reruns the same graph with the new model and the scene's current overrides. The scene reads what it renders from the group's named outputs (seamless, grid, patch surfaces) instead of engine fields.
9. Examination scenes that need only a prefix of the pipeline must not pay for all of it. Preferred: pull evaluation, where the runtime evaluates only the nodes a requested output depends on (Blender's model), so mcg-exam asks for layout's motorcycle output and quantization never runs. Acceptable alternative if pull evaluation proves too large for this ticket: each exam scene's graph calls the stage nodes it needs directly, and a follow-up ticket adds pull evaluation.
10. Setting inputs at run time. Overrides live on the scene (per path) and survive model switches; they are set through the model switch (`ixdar-cli model <name> --set layout/field.curvature_bias=-0.5`, repeatable) and a terminal `set` command, not through run-scene flags or system properties.

RELATED TICKETS. MESH-14 (Node Group System), MESH-13 (GroupInput/GroupOutput among control-flow nodes) and MESH-17 (hierarchical tree view) describe groups as a Java NodeGroup class serialized to JSON on top of MESH-3 (Node Graph Evaluation Engine, TODO). NodeGraphRuntime and DSL `def` already exist, so this ticket delivers MESH-14 items 1 to 4 and 6 and MESH-13's GroupInput/GroupOutput in DSL form, and its node tree is the structure MESH-17's tree view would display. TOOL-11 (ixdar-cli model) is the model-switch route that item 10 extends.

DECIDED 2026-09-26: one ticket, not split (the user treats it as an experiment that may be reverted). Nesting separator is `/` (`layout/field.curvature_bias`). The group library is plain .dsl files; SkillLibrary's front-matter .skill format (name, description, technique, fitness, generation, origin_run from an evolution-search run) goes, and subdivided_cube.skill becomes a .dsl group.

DECIDED 2026-09-26 (continued): mesh-viewer moves to the model/graph choice path in this ticket and the ixdar.mesh.dsl system property is removed from it (DungeonViewerScene's use of the property is out of scope). subdivided_cube.skill becomes a .dsl group and the .skill front-matter format is removed. Runs in parallel with PATCH-111 (block zero-arc collapse): if that lands first, sync and re-record the baseline. After this lands the coordinator closes MESH-14 (node groups) and the GroupInput/GroupOutput half of MESH-13; MESH-3 and MESH-17 stay open.
definition-of-done:
1. NodeGraphRuntime keeps a node tree: one record per evaluated node, including every node inside a group call at any depth (DSL-defined or compiled), with path (`/`-joined call-site ids), type, instance, inputs, outputs, ms and peak heap. Unit tests cover a two-level nested group.
2. Every node record holds the source of each input: the source node's path and port for a wired input, or the literal value. This holds for DSL statements, DSL group bodies, compiled group bodies and Java-built scene graphs alike, so a consumer (DSL-48's graph view) can draw boxes, literals and edges from the tree alone without parsing DSL text. Unit test over a DSL graph and a compiled group.
3. Groups declare parameters with defaults and several named outputs; callers read the outputs as ports. Existing DSL files, test_function.dsl and the DSL group library keep working unchanged.
4. Overrides are keyed by path plus port (`layout/field.curvature_bias`), reach nodes inside DSL and compiled groups, and an unknown path or port fails naming the nearest real paths. Unit tests cover both.
5. Compiled node groups: a NodeGroup base (a MeshNode) whose Java subclass declares its inner nodes and wiring through a group builder; the runtime, not the group, evaluates the inner nodes, so they appear in the tree with timing, accept path overrides and take part in pull evaluation. The rule "no MeshNode builds or evaluates another MeshNode" becomes "only through the group builder", enforced by the existing check.
6. The quad layout is a compiled group, QuadLayoutNode, registered as `quad_layout` so resources/dsl/fertility_quad_layout.dsl and DSL callers keep working. Its result is a typed QuadLayout object (cross field, seamless map, motorcycle graph, quantized skeleton, T-mesh, global grid map, patch surfaces) on one output port, with each stage also on its own named port. The DSL resource dsl/groups/quad_layout.dsl is removed. QuadLayoutEngine is removed or reduced to nothing that duplicates QuadLayout.
7. quad-layout, mcg-exam, cross-field-exam, param-exam, embedded-tmesh and mesh-viewer build their scene graphs in Java (the scene model input feeding QuadLayoutNode or the stage nodes); the dsl/scenes/*.dsl resources are removed. Model choice through the launch property, the menu, `ml` and `ixdar-cli model` keeps working in every one.
8. Exam scenes do not evaluate stages they do not show (pull evaluation).
9. `ixdar-cli node-inspect` prints the tree, one node, or a reflective field path on the active ModelScene's runtime, including inside compiled groups. /mesh/dsl/timing works on any ModelScene.
10. Scene overrides by path survive model switches and are set through `ixdar-cli model <name> --set <path>.<port>=<value>` (repeatable) and a terminal `set` command; no new run-scene flag and no system property.
11. Results are unchanged: bolt, hand, rockerarm, fandisk and buddha in one quad-layout JVM give the same meanDistortion, motorcycle arc/node/patch counts, quantize objective and embed counts as current master, recorded on the ticket.
12. The answer to 'what is trace N on bolt' comes from node-inspect with no source edit, shown on the ticket.

6. F5 each touched scene's launch entry and screenshot it.

Decided with the user 2026-10-17 (rework): the quad layout as a DSL text resource (dsl/groups/quad_layout.dsl) with QuadLayoutEngine as a typed view over it is the wrong way round. PATCH-57 (emit Coons-patch DSL from the layout) needs the quad layout as an object to work with, and every model scene loading a dsl/scenes/<id>.dsl resource for a two-line graph is indirection without benefit. Rework: compiled node groups (NodeGroup base + group builder; the runtime evaluates the inner nodes so the tree, timing, path overrides and pull evaluation all still apply), QuadLayoutNode as a compiled group registered as quad_layout with a typed QuadLayout result, scene graphs built in Java with the dsl/scenes resources removed. The DSL group library stays for hand-written groups. New requirement for DSL-48 (graph view): every node record holds each input's source (path+port or literal) so the view draws from the tree alone. Definition of done rewritten accordingly.

2026-10-17 rework (compiled groups). Synced onto 2f432bcb (CRAW-69 quantization, colours). NodeGroup (ixdar.geometry.mesh.graph, a MeshNode) + GroupBuilder: a subclass declares inner nodes in build(group), e.g. group.node("field", NDirectionField::new).input("geometry", group.parameter("geometry")) and group.output("field", field.port("field")); the builder emits the same ParsedNode statements the DSL parser does (ParsedNode gains supplier/input()/port()), so the runtime turns a compiled group into a FunctionDef once per run and evaluates the inner nodes itself: tree records with timing, path overrides (layout/field.curvature_bias), pull evaluation. Outputs the builder does not wire are computed by the group's evaluate() from the wired ones; the instance stays on the call's record. GroupBuilder.node(id, type) adds a registered node by id for web-reachable code. QuadLayoutNode (registered quad_layout, desktop-only) is the compiled group of field/seamless/motorcycle/quantize/embed/contract/assembly/relax/quads/surfaces with ports geometry, uv, tmesh, field, singularities, seamless, motorcycle, skeleton, embedded, surfaces, coons, plus layout: a typed QuadLayout (new PortType.QUAD_LAYOUT) holding crossField, seamless, motorcycle, skeleton, tmesh, globalGrid, quads, patchSurfaces, patchCoons. QuadLayoutEngine is gone; QuadLayout is its field set without the build* methods. dsl/groups/quad_layout.dsl and dsl/scenes/*.dsl removed; ModelScene.sceneGraph() returns Java-built statements, and quad-layout, mcg-exam, cross-field-exam, param-exam, embedded-tmesh return QuadLayoutNode.overSceneModel() (model = scene_model(); layout = quad_layout(geometry=model.geometry)) and pull only what they draw; QuadLayoutScene holds one QuadLayout (SeamlessDiagnosis reads scene.layout.seamless). Input sources: GraphNodeContext.inputSources (and outputSources on group calls) hold a NodeReference(source path, port) for a wired input, a group parameter being (group path, parameter), else the literal/override/default; node-inspect shows them as input_sources. Tests/benchmarks moved onto the layout graph (pull of named ports, layout/<node>.<port> for counters). MeshNodeIndependenceTest: a node may take another node's constructor only as group.node(id, X::new) inside a NodeGroup. NodeGraphTreeTest +2 (input sources over a DSL graph; compiled group SumAndProductGroup: records, pull, computed output, override, nearest path).
